title: Ramji Lal v. Govind Das
text: The landlord, Ramji Lal, filed an eviction petition against the tenant, Govind Das, under the Rajasthan Rent Control Act on the ground of default in payment of rent and subletting without consent. The tenancy was established by a registered rent deed. The tenant claimed to be a protected tenant entitled to protection under the Rent Control Act. Evidence showed that the tenant had been in arrears of rent for over 24 months. The landlord duly demanded rent and issued legal notices. The claim of protected tenant status was negatived as the original tenancy was created after the threshold date under the Rent Control Act. The court grants the eviction decree against the tenant. The landlord is entitled to vacant possession. The tenant is directed to pay arrears of rent of Rs 3,60,000 within 60 days. Eviction is granted on grounds of default in rent payment under the Rent Control Act.
